stories.headline: 10 missing, 6 rescued as flash flood hits Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River
stories.title: 10 missing, 6 rescued as flash flood hits Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River
stories.summary: Kathmandu [Nepal], October 11 : At least 10 people have been unaccounted for since Sunday morning following flooding along the Budhi Gandaki River basin in Gorkha District, Nepal, officials confirmed. The flood also swept away six bridges, including two motorable bridges and four suspension bridges. Assistant Chief District Officer Netra Prasad Sharma told ANI over the phone that the flood destroyed the motorable bridges at Arughat, Tripurasundari and Soti-Manbu. A Bailey bridge connecting wards 1 and 3 of Dharche Rural Municipality in Gorkha was also swept away by the floodwaters. Other bridges damaged or destroyed in the disaster include footbridges connecting Machhikhola with Karauja, Thadobharyang with Jagat, and Ghattekhola with Philim. “In addition, 10 people have been reported missing since the flood hit the northern part of the district earlier this morning. An alert is in place as the river’s water level has continued to rise and fall. We are constantly monitoring the flow,” Sharma told ANI. The flood swept away nearly 35 houses in Painyu and Bagar in Ward 3 of Chumnubri Rural Municipality. It also damaged settlements in Jagat, Salleri, Dovan and Ghattekhola. Following the incident, Prime Minister (PM) Balen Shah said a Nepali Army contingent had been deployed by air and land to conduct search and rescue operations. He added that helicopters had been mobilised to support rescue, relief and evacuation efforts in the Budhi Gandaki flood-affected region. A Joint Rapid Response Team from Kathmandu has also been airlifted to the area to assist with the response. An hour later, the Nepal Army announced that six people had been evacuated to safer areas from the flood-affected region, which lies about 184 kilometres from the capital, Kathmandu. Taking to social media, Home Minister Sudan Gurung warned of another severe flood in Nepal following a surge in the Budhi Gandaki River in Gorkha on Sunday morning. In a social media post accompanying a video of the flooding, Gurung said security personnel, including helicopter teams, had been mobilised to the affected areas for rescue, relief and evacuation operations. “Nepal has faced another severe flood, and I have been seriously concerned by reports that the bridge connecting Nyakchet and Film Bazaar in Ward No. 3 of Chumanubri Rural Municipality, Gorkha, has been washed away. The river’s flow is continuously increasing, and muddy floodwaters have entered some houses in the Ghattekhola area,” he wrote. He added that helicopters had been deployed immediately after the incident, while the Nepal Police, Armed Police Force and local administration had been mobilised to carry out rescue and relief operations and move people to safety. The Home Minister urged residents of Sirdibas, Jagat, Salleri, Khorlabesi, Machhakhola, Soti, Arkhet and Arughat, particularly those living along the banks of the Budhi Gandaki River, to relocate to safer areas without delay and remain on high alert. “I sincerely request residents of these areas, especially those living along the Budhi Gandaki River, to move to safer places immediately and remain highly alert. Please remain calm and stay safe,” Gurung wrote. He also urged people requiring emergency assistance to contact the Ministry of Home Affairs on 1234. (ANI)

stories.headline: New Deputy Election Commissioner appointed in ECI amid concerns over work hierarchy
stories.title: New Deputy Election Commissioner appointed in ECI amid concerns over work hierarchy
stories.summary: Prakash Rajpurohit fills the vacancy left by Sanjay Kumar’s premature repatriation, amid concerns raised by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over IT department files not being routed through him
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Prakash Rajpurohit, an IAS officer of the 2010 batch, has been appointed as a Deputy Election Commissioner in the Election Commission of India (ECI), filling the vacancy caused by the premature repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, who was incharge of the Electoral Rolls and IT division.

What will be the work allocation in the ECI after this new appointment is crucial, as Sanjay Kumar, who had been DEC from August 2024 till August this year, had been responsible for the electoral roll and IT divisions of the ECI, and had signed the ECI’s June 24, 2025, order initiating the SIR in the country.
It is also important because the two Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written to the Cabinet Secretary on how files of the ECI.
IT department head Dr. Seema Khanna not being routed through Mr. Kumar, who was a seasoned officer, was a violation.
Dr. Khanna joined the ECI in 2025 on deputation from the National Informatics Centre.
She heads the commission’s.
IT department, and oversees its digital infrastructure, including systems for electoral-roll management.

According to Election Commission sources, before the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar to his parent cadre, Dr. Khanna’s files had been routed through him till she was given a promotion to Level 15, which is equivalent to the rank of an Additional Secretary.

Since Mr. Kumar was of the rank of a Joint Secretary (which is Level 14), Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg issued an internal order that Dr. Khanna’s files should go straight to the Election Commissioners from then.
This order was, however, never implemented.

Dr. Khanna’s files started being routed through to Maneesh Garg himself following the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, as he was his link officer, which made him responsible for his departments in his absence.
Mr. Rajpurohit’s appointment was cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet late on Saturday as per the order by the Department of Personnel and Training.

stories.headline: Protests in Delhi: SC directs no illegal detention, restoration of internet and metro services
stories.title: Protests in Delhi: SC directs no illegal detention, restoration of internet and metro services
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 11: The Supreme Court on Sunday directed that people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained, as it issued a notice to the Centre on a plea seeking contempt proceedings for alleged violation of the court's direction to ensure that there is no "complete prohibition" on metro and train services in Delhi due to the CJP protest. In a special sitting, a bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure that Delhi Metro functions as per its normal schedule, and that there is no disruption to internet services, subject to law and order conditions. "In view of the urgent applications alleging violation of our earlier order dt. October 9, 2026, and also alleging illegal detention of large number of individuals at Delhi on October 10, 2026 this court had assembled for an urgent hearing. "Senior counsels submitted there was a flagrant violation of the directions -- metro railway was not functioning, New Delhi and Nizamuddin railway stations remained closed, no traffic advisories were issued and a large number of persons were subjected to undue harassment and illegal detention even beyond the area which was covered by the prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023," the bench said. The apex court also asked Mehta to ensure that lawyers, journalists and others shall not be impeded in discharging their professional duties. During the hearing, Mehta submitted that entry and exit were restricted at only 45 out of 303 stations across the metro network on October 10. As the hearing commenced, the top court said it would grant hearing to all lawyers while dealing with a plea seeking contempt proceedings against authorities for alleged blatant violation of the court's direction on the matter. The top court was also hearing a habeas petition filed by senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy against the detention of political leaders. The contempt plea, filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, has arrayed Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation chairperson D Thara as respondents. The petition referred to the top court's October 9 order, which was passed while hearing a separate plea against the closure of 57 metro stations and cancellation of trains to Delhi in view of the protest. The protest call was given by the CJP and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission. The government thwarted a planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on Saturday after an unprecedented security clampdown and the detention of over 7,000 protesters, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.

article_sentences: Kapil Sibal welcomed the Supreme Court's directions on handling the Delhi protests.
The order addressed detentions, transport and professional access, reinforcing faith in the justice system.
Rajya Sabha MP and senior advocate Kapil Sibal on Sunday welcomed the Supreme Court’s directions on protests in Delhi, saying the order had restored faith in the country’s justice system.
He said the ruling reassured both the public and professionals.
The Supreme Court directed that people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained.
It also asked the Centre to ensure that Delhi Metro services run on their normal schedule and that internet services remain uninterrupted, subject to law and order conditions.

"We are deeply grateful to the Supreme Court of India for passing an order that restores the faith of the Indian people, as well as the faith of professionals, in the justice system of this country," Sibal said.
A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also said lawyers, journalists and others should not be stopped from carrying out their professional duties.

The court issued notice to the Centre on a plea seeking contempt proceedings against the authorities for allegedly violating its October 9 order on restrictions on Metro and train services in Delhi in view of the protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and some student organisations.

The applications before the court alleged that Metro services were disrupted, New Delhi and Nizamuddin railway stations remained closed, and a large number of people faced harassment and illegal detention on October 10.
The protest had been called against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.

Authorities had detained over 7,000 protesters, including CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, during a security clampdown aimed at preventing the planned mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on Saturday.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Acquits Man In POCSO Case Over Victim's Failure To Identify Him In Court, Unexplained Delay In FIR
stories.title: Supreme Court Acquits Man In POCSO Case Over Victim's Failure To Identify Him In Court, Unexplained Delay In FIR
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta set aside the concurrent findings of the trial court and the Meghalaya High Court.
It found that the evidence of the victim's mother (informant), the victim and the victim's cousin was wavering and unreliable.

It is alleged that the appellant sexually assaulted the 40% intellectually disabled victim in 2015 when she was 11 years old, at her home when her mother (informant/PW 1) had gone out and she was alone.
PW 1 allegedly saw the accused plucking mulberry leaves in the garden next to the house as she left.
Thereafter, the victim then went to her cousin's house (PW 2) and stayed for the night.
The cousin told the victim's mother about the incident the next day, but the mother did not take it seriously because the child did not confirm the accusation.
Later, the victim disclosed the incident to her school teacher who informed the parents and an FIR was lodged nearly 10 days after the alleged incident.
The accused was then convicted by Special Judge (POCSO) and was sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 Lakh.
The accused appealed before the High Court which dismissed his appeal in 2022.
Aggrieved by the High Court's dismissal, the appellant approached the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, Senior Advocate Gaurav Agrawal argued for the appellant (accused) that the prosecution had failed to explain the delay of nearly ten days in lodging the FIR.

It was submitted that PW 2 (victim's cousin) had told PW 1 (victim's mother/informant) about the incident on the very next day, yet this fact was not mentioned in the FIR, and the mother took no recourse to police action or medical assistance, which would have been the natural reaction had the allegations been true.

The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognizance of recent cases of rape in Delhi-NCR, including a gangrape in a park and the alleged sexual assault of a minor inside a moving sleeper bus in Delhi.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran observed that they were distressed by the news reports regarding recurring sexual offences in the National Capital Region, and stressed the need to fix accountability.
In the order, the bench referred to the gangrape and murder of a teenage girl in Swarup Nagar in Delhi, where the police recovered the victim's decomposed body in a field.

Referring to the sexual assault of a minor in a moving sleeping bus, which the police failed to intercept during its travel of 47 kilometres from Greater Noida to Delhi, the Court said that “one cannot help but draw painful parallels to the Nirbhaya incident of 2012.”
The Supreme Court on Monday (September 28) issued a set of immediate directions to the Delhi.
Police and civic authorities to secure public spaces in Delhi-NCR.
The directions include a survey of vulnerable areas, a district-wise vulnerability map, patrolling at all identified parks, and a lighting and CCTV audit.
All are to be completed within four weeks.
